name: Michigan

governingStatutes.name: Michigan Workers' Disability Compensation Act
governingStatutes.scope: Employers with 3+ employees or 1+ for 35+ hrs/week for 13+ weeks

administeringAgency.name: Workers' Disability Compensation Agency (WDCA)
administeringAgency.parentAgency: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity

covered: Employers with 1+ employee working 35+ hrs/week for 13+ weeks
Agricultural employers with 3+ employees or $35k+ payroll
excluded: Domestic servants in homes with <2 employees

benefitCategories.medical: Reasonable and necessary treatment; employer may direct care for first 28 days
benefitCategories.wageLoss: 80% of after-tax wages up to 90% of state average weekly wage ($1,088/week 2024); until age 65 or 5 years from disability (whichever later)
benefitCategories.specificLoss: Schedule for amputations, loss of hearing/sight (weeks × comp rate)
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 80% of after-tax wages to dependents; up to 500 weeks; $6,000 burial

appealLevels.name: Magistrate Hearing
appealLevels.deadline: 2 years from injury or last payment

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: WDCA dispute resolution; fraud investigation; carrier compliance
workersCompensation.penalties: Late payment penalties; self-insured revocation; fraud prosecution

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Michigan has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: Healthy Michigan Plan (Expanded Medicaid)
programs.administeringBody: Michigan Dept. of Health and Human Services
programs.eligibility: Adults 19-64 with income up to 138% FPL; Michigan expanded Medicaid

statutes.name: Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act
statutes.protections: Disability discrimination prohibited; race, religion, color, national origin, sex, height, weight, familial status, marital status

statutes.name: Persons with Disabilities Civil Rights Act
statutes.protections: Specific disability protections; accommodation required; broader than federal

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for filing complaints, participating in proceedings, or opposing violations

accommodationObligations.standard: Reasonable accommodation under PWDCRA; undue hardship defense

enablingStatutes.disability: No state TDI; Public Assistance statutes

laborStandards.authority: Wage and Hour Act; Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act

civilRights.deadline: 180 days for PWDCRA; 3 years for Elliott-Larsen (civil action)

occupationalSafety.authority: Michigan OSHA Act; state plan state covering public and private sector

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 2 years from injury or last compensation payment
filingDeadlines.civilRightsLawsuit: 3 years under Elliott-Larsen (no exhaustion required for civil suits)

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; wage loss focus (not impairment ratings alone)
evidentiaryStandards.civilRights: Prima facie case; McDonnell Douglas burden-shifting

judicialReview.wc: Magistrate → WCAC → Court of Appeals → Supreme Court
judicialReview.civilRights: MDCR (optional) → Circuit Court → Court of Appeals
judicialReview.directFiling: No requirement to exhaust MDCR before filing lawsuit under Elliott-Larsen

specialConsiderations.wageLossSystem: Michigan is a 'wage loss' state—benefits focus on actual earnings loss, not impairment ratings
specialConsiderations.coordinationWithSsdi: WC benefits may be reduced if combined with SSDI exceeds 80% of pre-injury wages
specialConsiderations.mioshaCoverage: Michigan is a state plan state with MIOSHA covering both public and private employers
specialConsiderations.sexualOrientationAddition2023: 2023 interpretation/amendment added sexual orientation and gender identity to Elliott-Larsen
